newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban cross strategic Salang Pass.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban cross strategic Salang Pass.

text.p: The Taleban Islamic militia, in tanks and other vehicles, crossed the strategic Salang Pass in northern Afghanistan on Tuesday after being blocked for two days by enemy shelling, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted its sources in Afghanistan as saying that the Taleban crossed the Salang Pass but their advance further north was held up by a blown-up bridge about five km (three miles) north of the pass. There was no independent confirmation of the report.
The AIP said some Taleban troops continued to march on foot and reached the village of Khinjan in Baghlan province, about 15 km (nine miles) north of the Salang pass.

Taleban control of the pass will cut off the last link between the ousted government's top military commander Ahmed Shah Masood, who controls pockets of northeastern Afghanistan, and Hezb-i-Wahadat, a mainly Shi'ite faction still fighting to retain control of central Afghanistan's Bamiyan province.

The Taleban had reached the 11,000-feet (3,350 m) long gateway, north of the capital Kabul, on Sunday, seeking to cross into opposition territory after a peace deal with a local pro-Masood commander, Basir Salangi.
But they were held up by opposition resistance.
